newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO firmer, SIMEX Dec up 70 cents.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO firmer, SIMEX Dec up 70 cents.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Thursday were assessed marginally stronger, supported by bullish crude oil prices but capped by unsold supplies, traders said.

High sulphur 180 centistoke (cst) fuel oil cargoes were bid/offered at $120/$121 per tonne for early December loading supplies on a free-on-board basis from Singaoie, slightly higher than Wednesday's offer of $120.50.
A Dutch trader who was seen offering barrels on Wednesday said he may offer the cargoes again later Thursday.
The trader said prices may edge up slightly on crude but the market's upside is limited as there were still unsold supplies.
Traders said although Chinese buyers have emerged to enquire for December barrels, there was a lack of genuine buying interest.
"They were just making enquiries," a trader said.
A Chinese trader in Hong Kong said he had already purchased a total of four cargoes from South Korea for end November to early December loading.

Traders said a fall in the weekly residue stock figures released by the Singapore Trade Development Board have also firmed sentiment. Residue stocks fell by 507,000 barrels, to 11.107 million barrels.

Swaps levels were however unaffected with November and December at $119.50/$120.25 and $118.00/$119.00 respectively, little moved from Wednesday quotes. December was traded at $118.50 and $118.75, brokers said.
The SIMEX fuel oil December futures contract was traded 70 cents firmer at $119 per tonne with a total of 10 lots seen done at 0807 GMT.
